messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @ryan - GPU node gpu-az2-17 reporting repeated Xid 13/31 driver resets and ECC corrected/unrecovered errors. Multiple inference containers restarted in the last 3m. Please acknowledge and triage.

maria: acked. I'm on it, grabbing logs now. tagging @julia for customer impact (AcmeCorp running critical rollout).

ryan: I saw the alert. jumping in. First glance: kernel shows nv-host reset followed by container oom kills for the runtime. attaching quick `dmesg` excerpt.

ryan: ```
[2234567801.123] NVRM: Xid (13) at 0xdeadbeef
[2234567801.124] NVRM: GPU 0000:3b:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[2234567802.000] kernel: Task cloud-infer-1234: Out of memory: Killed process 3942 (python)
```

julia: thanks. cs-lead, Acme is reporting increased 5xxs on their /predict route since ~04:20 UTC. They hit our SLA alert. Can we confirm percentage?

cs-lead: confirming, we're seeing ~12% 5xx across their traffic, mostly internal 502/504 from inference nodes. They're in prod, mid-sized volume. Not yet escalated but monitoring.

maria: mitigation steps: cordon gpu-az2-17, drain with graceful terminate for pods that support fallback. I'll start canary routing to dedicated pool gpu-dedicated-1.

sam: good call. We should also flip the fallback policy for the affected model to `low-latency-fallback-v2` so requests go to a lower-util but compatible variant. Doing that now via console API.

infra-bot: command accepted: `kubectl cordon gpu-az2-17` executed by maria at 2234567830. Drain initiated: `kubectl drain gpu-az2-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60`

ryan: looking at telemetry: ECC corrected spikes correlate with host thermal events on that rack. We have multiple GPUs showing corrected ECC counts rising quickly, then an Xid reset. Suspect a transient power/thermal on rack pdu.

maria: noting action: cordoned/drain in progress. moving live traffic off node. Can we confirm if any other nodes in the same rack show similar symptoms?

ryan: yes, gpu-az2-18 has small ECC uptick but stable. I'll run `nvidia-smi -q` across the rack and dump ECC counters.

ryan: ```bash
for n in gpu-az2-{17,18,19}; do ssh $n "nvidia-smi -q | grep -E 'ECC|Xid' -n"; done
```

julia: CS update: Acme's on a call, asking whether we are degrading quality or just shifting traffic. Told them we're routing to a healthy pool and expect <1 min impact after graceful drains finish.

sam: fallback flip succeeded. Traffic steering shows 85% of new requests routed to gpu-dedicated-1, 15% to fallback. Error rate dropping from 12% -> 3% in last 2m.

maria: drain finished for non-daemonset pods. Some long-running streams kept sockets open and triggered retries; we restarted those pods explicitly.

infra-bot: log snapshot uploaded to s3://redwood-incidents/2234567890/gpu-az2-17-logs.tar.gz by ryan.

ryan: I want to reboot the host after we finish evacuation to clear driver state and run hardware diagnostics. Propose privileged restart: `sudo systemctl reboot` after final pod eviction. Any objections?

julia: go ahead. Coordinate with oncall-bot for maintenance window. CS will notify Acme that we'll perform a host reboot as a precaution.

maria: performing post-evac validation: running load test on gpu-dedicated-1 to ensure latency SLOs hold. So far p95 is stable at 120ms.

cs-lead: Acme on the call appreciated the proactive routing. They're asking for a postmortem and whether their data was ever exposed (no). We told them no data plane changes, only routing.

sam: note: model quantization config for the fallback variant differs slightly; outputs validated against unit prompts, minor diff in tokenization but within tolerance. Logging this as potential regression.

ryan: host reboot done. After reboot, drivers loaded cleanly. `nvidia-smi` shows ECC counters cleared but one card still reports marginal ECC corrected rate on slot 3. I'll schedule a replacement for that GPU.

maria: switching node back to schedulable after hardware replacement plan confirmed? We should keep it cordoned until replacement.

ryan: leaving it cordoned. I've opened infra ticket INF-4527 for hardware swap and attached diagnostics. ETA replacement 48h due to spare inventory.

infra-bot: ticket INF-4527 created by ryan: "gpu-az2-17 slot3 intermittent ECC/Xid causing driver resets - hw swap requested"

julia: Current customer impact: Acme errors down to 0.8% and decreasing. We'll continue monitoring for 2h per SLA. CS flagged for follow-up email to customer summarizing actions.

maria: follow-up checklist: 1) keep node cordoned until swap 2) add rack PDU telemetry alert 3) run broader ECC baseline sweep across AZ2 4) include a note in postmortem about fallback/regression check.

sam: adding automated test to our rollout pipeline to run smoke-check against fallback model variants next week.

ryan: final note: root cause likely transient power/thermal event causing ECC spike -> driver panic/Xid -> container OOM cascade. Hardware replacement + PDU telemetry should prevent recurrence.

julia: thanks team. I'll draft the incident summary and ping for postmortem contributors. Closing the active paging thread; will reopen if new Xid events appear. :white_check_mark:
